title: Let parallel coding agents ship your site through one queue
summary: Bret Kerr ran 8 Claude Code sessions on his website; when deploys jammed, Claude designed a pipeline where each agent opens a change and GitHub merges them one by one.
agent_role: Claude Code sessions built features in parallel and then proposed and packaged the deploy process as a reusable skill. The author asked the question and chose the approach.
outcome: Author says six lanes now feed one pipeline and 'the inbox empties itself.'
what_they_did: Bret Kerr had 8 Claude Code sessions building parts of his website at once, like a search bar and a book chapter. They all deployed from his laptop and waited on each other. He asked Claude for a better way. Now each session works on its own copy, runs checks, opens a change request, and checks its own preview page.
how_it_went: He reports GitHub now merges changes one at a time, and each merge goes live on Cloudflare. Claude turned the rules into a skill so future sessions follow them automatically.
worth_knowing: The original snag was that every agent deployed from one laptop, so one sat idle waiting for another's build to finish.
prompt: I run several coding agent sessions on [repo URL] at once, and they block each other when deploying. Design a workflow where each session works on its own branch in a separate folder, runs the checks locally, opens a pull request, and checks its own preview link. Merges to main should happen one at a time and go live on [hosting service]. Show me the plan and any settings changes before applying them. Then write the rules down as a reusable instruction file future sessions will follow.

curation.rationale: A real setup with 8 parallel Claude Code sessions and a concrete fix for deploy bottlenecks. The steps are listed but no numbers or code are shared.
